editorial:
Imagine spending a whole day just following a guy around the city as he does his normal chores. That is exactly how you start this journey. You get to see him run errands and talk to people, but something feels off from the very beginning. The mood is kind of tense, and you can tell that the world around him is not quite right. It feels like a puzzle where you only get one piece at a time, making you wonder why everyone seems so on edge and what is actually happening behind the scenes.

What really works here is how the tension builds up slowly until it finally hits you. The acting is solid and makes the city feel real and lived-in. While the slow start might bore some people, the payoff at the end is totally worth the wait. If you enjoy stories that make you think and keep you guessing, you should definitely check this out. It looks great in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, but if you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a smart move for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: The movie ends by showing that the main character is living in a city ruined by war. All those weird routines and quiet moments were actually his way of coping with a huge tragedy. The big twist is that the world has already collapsed, and he is just trying to find a way to survive in the wreckage. It wraps up by showing that the crisis is not coming, but has already happened.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves slow mysteries and emotional stories about survival.
